records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Teresa represents the soul as an interior castle with multiple rooms or mansions.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Prayer and recollection function as the gate and discipline for entering deeper levels of interior life.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Self-knowledge is treated as necessary for understanding the soul's relation to God.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: The mansions distinguish progressively different states of prayer, attention and union.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Movement through the mansions represents a progressive transformation of the subject.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: The deepest mansion is described in terms of union with God rather than simple accumulation of knowledge.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: The practitioner must learn to distinguish wandering imagination from deeper forms of prayer.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Humility, love and detachment are treated as markers of a well-ordered spiritual trajectory.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Teresa repeatedly connects mystical states with bodily effects while refusing to identify the soul with those effects.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Higher states are described as difficult to communicate and vulnerable to misunderstanding.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: The architecture of the mansions makes transformation explicitly developmental and sequential.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Mystical death and longing for God are used as metaphors for relinquishing ordinary self-orientation.

records.location: Interior Castle, First–Seventh Mansions; prayer, self-knowledge and union
records.claim: Interior Castle is a sixteenth-century Christian mystical testimony and should not be treated as empirical evidence of altered consciousness.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The dark night is presented as a purgative process intended to prepare the soul for union.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: John distinguishes novice, proficient and perfected states along the spiritual path.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: Active detachment and discipline precede or accompany passive purification.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The purification targets sensory and spiritual faculties within the person.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The practitioner is asked to recognize the limits and attachments of ordinary knowing and desiring.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: Darkness is paradoxically treated as a condition that can prepare greater light and freedom.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The deepest contemplation is described as darkness precisely because it exceeds ordinary conceptual understanding.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The trajectory culminates in union of love with God rather than in a new catalogue of concepts.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The work distinguishes discursive meditation from more passive contemplative awareness.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: Purgation is described as a dynamic process in which faculties lose habitual attachments and are reordered.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The two nights introduce a staged progression through different forms of purification.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The language of dying to self and to created attachments functions as a transformation of identity rather than literal destruction.

records.location: Books I–II; active/passive purgation, contemplation and union
records.claim: The Dark Night is a theological-mystical account of Christian spiritual formation, not a modern clinical model of cognition.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The soul's transformation is expressed through a relational image of bride and Bridegroom.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The canticle differentiates longing, search, encounter, repose and consummation as distinct experiential conditions.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: Desire is progressively reoriented toward union rather than ordinary possession.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The search for the Beloved is simultaneously an inward movement of the soul.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: Contemplation, recollection and detachment support the journey represented by the poem.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The soul learns to recognize traces of the Beloved in creation and in its own interior life.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The culmination is framed as a unitive knowledge and love in which separation is radically reduced.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: Love, desire and peaceful rest provide the main evaluative orientation of the journey.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: Poetic symbols are used because the contemplated relation is not adequately captured by literal description.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The poem preserves a narrative of seeking, finding and deepening union.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: Images of sleep, touch, wounds, scent and landscape connect bodily imagery with spiritual transformation.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The soul's yearning can include desire for death as release into fuller union with the Beloved.

records.location: Spiritual Canticle, stanzas on bride, bridegroom, contemplation and transformation
records.claim: The text is a Christian mystical poem and its experiential language should not be universalized without historical qualification.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Böhme describes reality through a dynamic relation between divine ground, manifestation and natural qualities.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Opposed qualities and forces are treated as necessary to the emergence of differentiated manifestation.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Multiplicity is repeatedly related back to an underlying divine ground.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Nature functions as an arena in which spiritual principles become manifest and legible.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Human beings can investigate the same dynamic principles within themselves.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Inner experience is treated as a locus where divine and natural dynamics become perceivable.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Awakening involves movement from obscurity toward recognition of the divine source within created existence.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Light and darkness, good and evil, and attraction and resistance are interpreted within a larger dynamic theology.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Human embodiment is not excluded from the spiritual drama but participates in the manifestation of principles.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Natural qualities can signify or correspond to spiritual structures in Böhme's symbolic cosmology.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: The soul can be represented as undergoing different conditions according to which principle dominates its orientation.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: The divine ground is described through paradoxical language because it exceeds ordinary conceptual representation.

records.location: Aurora: first principles, nature, divine manifestation, polarity and inner awakening
records.claim: Aurora is an early modern Christian theosophical work whose cosmology should be distinguished from later scientific theories of nature or mind.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Böhme treats visible forms and qualities as signs or signatures of deeper spiritual principles.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Nature is described as containing an interior or spiritual dimension not exhausted by outward appearance.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Learning to read signatures requires an interpreter who attends to relationships between visible and invisible orders.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Discernment of signatures functions as a contemplative and interpretive discipline.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: The capacity to perceive inner significance depends on the spiritual condition and orientation of the observer.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Material bodies and qualities are treated as vehicles through which hidden properties can appear.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: The interaction of forces within nature gives rise to signs that reveal the quality of underlying processes.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: External and internal orders remain connected through systematic correspondence.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Natural things are interpreted in relation to beneficial or harmful qualities and spiritual orientation.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: The knower's relation to nature changes when visible forms are understood as expressions of deeper principles.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Close observation is necessary to distinguish a mere appearance from a meaningful signature.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: Hidden principles require symbolic language because their full nature is not directly available to ordinary perception.

records.location: De Signatura Rerum; signatures, nature, inner qualities and correspondence
records.claim: De Signatura Rerum belongs to Böhme's theosophical system and its doctrine of signatures is historical/esoteric rather than established natural science.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Otto distinguishes the numinous as a distinctive state of consciousness rather than ordinary conceptual knowledge.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Awe, fascination and dread form a characteristic evaluative structure of numinous experience.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: The numinous cannot be fully defined propositionally and must be approached through analogy and contrast.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Religious experience is analyzed through changes occurring within consciousness and feeling.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: The subject is guided to notice analogous experiences within their own mental life in order to grasp the numinous.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Otto's method deliberately directs attention toward distinctive affective and experiential features.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: The numinous concerns the subject's relation to what is experienced as mysteriously beyond the ordinary self.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Otto resists reducing the holy to any one rational or ethical category, preserving a complex experiential whole.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Mysterium tremendum and fascination describe different but related poles of the same experiential encounter.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Encounter with the numinous is treated as capable of reshaping the subject's religious orientation.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Otto distinguishes historical developmental forms of the holy while preserving a recurring experiential core.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: The experiencing subject is not presented as a detached observer but as affectively involved in the numinous encounter.

records.location: Chapters II–VI and later analysis of numinous experience
records.claim: Otto's phenomenological-theological analysis describes religious experience; it does not establish an ontological proof of supernatural entities.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Swedenborg interprets natural forms, human interiors and spiritual realities through systematic correspondences.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: He describes spiritual and divine life as flowing through ordered levels into natural and bodily manifestations.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Human interiors of understanding, will and memory are treated as distinct dimensions of an internal person.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: The internal and external human are connected through affection, thought and action.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: End, cause and effect are linked in a sequence through which spiritual purposes become natural actions.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Regeneration is described as bringing interior and exterior levels into greater correspondence.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Different states of affection, thought and life correspond to different degrees of spiritual alignment.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Body, senses, speech and action are treated as external expressions of internal states.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Love, charity, truth and their opposites are used to evaluate whether correspondence is healthy or distorted.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: The internal sense of scripture is also a method for re-reading one's own inner condition.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Swedenborg's anthropology includes a doctrine of continuity of the inner person beyond bodily death.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Human nature and the broader spiritual world are mapped onto one another as nested correspondences.

records.location: Arcana Coelestia; internal sense, correspondences, influx and regeneration
records.claim: Arcana Coelestia is an eighteenth-century theological exegesis and should be separated from modern empirical theories of mind.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Swedenborg describes heaven and the natural world as related domains with systematic correspondences.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: The inner person is represented as continuous with a spiritual environment after bodily death.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Heavenly societies and individual beings are differentiated by states of love, intention and understanding.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Objects and events in the natural world are treated as signs of spiritual realities.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Personhood is fundamentally relational, shaped by community and the dominant loves of the individual.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: The post-mortem trajectory is presented as a continuation and clarification of the person's ruling loves.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Understanding and will are treated as core interior faculties that structure the person's spiritual life.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: The body is the natural level through which interior affections and thoughts become externally manifest.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Love of self, love of the world and love of the divine are treated as competing organizing orientations.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: States after death are described as developments of dispositions already formed during earthly life.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Heaven is repeatedly portrayed as an ordered whole whose parts reflect a single human form.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Learning spiritual meaning involves looking beyond surface appearances toward correspondential structures.

records.location: Heaven and Hell; spiritual world, correspondence, states after death and personhood
records.claim: Heaven and Hell presents a nineteenth-century reception of Swedenborgian theology, not an empirically verified map of an afterlife.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The Qur'an uses nafs to speak about the self or person in contexts of responsibility, desire and moral change.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The heart (qalb) is repeatedly associated with understanding, responsiveness, and moral orientation.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The human being is depicted as capable of self-examination, self-reproach and purification.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Ruh is used in several distinct Qur'anic contexts and should not be collapsed into a single modern notion of consciousness.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The text differentiates states such as remembrance, heedlessness, gratitude, hardness and tranquility of the heart.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Remembrance, prayer, recitation and ethical action function as practices for reorienting the person.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Repentance and purification are represented as processes through which the person changes moral and spiritual condition.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: God-consciousness, justice, gratitude and mercy form central evaluative axes for human action.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Remembrance and heedfulness emphasize sustained orientation of attention toward God and moral accountability.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Human identity is defined through relation to God, other people, creation and one's own acts.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The Qur'an links present action with future accountability, creating a temporally extended moral self-model.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: Creation is presented within a unified divine sovereignty while preserving distinctions among creatures.

records.location: Qur'an; nafs, qalb, ruh, remembrance, perception and moral transformation
records.claim: The Qur'an is a foundational Islamic scripture whose vocabulary of nafs, qalb and ruh must be read contextually rather than translated into one technical consciousness construct.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Hadith Qudsi often frame spiritual life as an intimate relationship between God and the devoted servant.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Obligatory and supererogatory acts are presented as a graded path of approach to God.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Continued practice is described as changing the servant's relation to God and the way action is experienced.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: One major tradition expresses divine nearness through the servant's hearing, seeing, hand and foot as metaphors of aligned agency.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: The servant moves from ordinary devotion toward a state characterized by divine love and protection.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Devotion, love, sincerity and obedience have positive normative status within the corpus.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: The graded practice model implies sustained orientation rather than isolated acts of remembrance.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: The individual remains a servant with personal agency while becoming more deeply aligned with divine will.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: The divine-human relation is reciprocal in idiom: devotion elicits divine favor, love and response.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: One Qudsi tradition explicitly speaks about the servant's soul and reluctance to die, integrating mortality into the devotional model.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Repeated practice is presented as a process in which proximity and love increase rather than remain static.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: Hearing, seeing and acting are symbolically unified around one devotional orientation rather than treated as disconnected faculties.

records.location: Selected Qudsi traditions; divine-human proximity, worship, love, hearing and action
records.claim: The hadith qudsi corpus is transmitted through individual hadith reports of differing chains and grades; claims must therefore remain report-specific.
